media:group.media:title: Can you tell someone is lying just by looking at them? #AskCaltech
NOM4D – ASTRA Assembly Demonstration
media:group.media:description:
A robotic truss builder that was conceived, designed, and built by Caltech researchers and funded by the Defense Advanced Research Projects Agency (DARPA) has successfully built a structure in space—without the help of astronauts—for the first time.
"This is the first time that a structure has been autonomously constructed in space," says Sergio Pellegrino, team leader of Caltech's Autonomous In-Space Tensioned Reflector Assembly (ASTRA) demonstration.
This video shows an earth-bound version of ASTRA building the 1.4-meter-diameter reflector antenna from composite fiber tubes, and aluminum joints in Pellegino's Caltech laboratory.
More info: https://www.caltech.edu/about/news/caltech-robotic-space-demo-successfully-builds-in-space

entry.title: Career-Defining Relationships with Tara Gomez-Hampton (PhD '11) | Caltech Career Conversations

media:group.media:title: Career-Defining Relationships with Tara Gomez-Hampton (PhD '11) | Caltech Career Conversations
media:group.media:description:
Technical expertise can open doors, but what determines where your career goes next? In this episode of Caltech Career Conversations, Tara Gomez-Hampton (PhD '11), director of medical affairs at Johnson & Johnson MedTech, explores how professional relationships, persistence, and unexpected opportunities have shaped her career beyond the lab. Tara shares insights on navigating career transitions, recognizing opportunities outside your immediate field, and building connections that can influence your professional trajectory. Whether you're exploring career possibilities, considering a new direction, or looking to advance in your field, this conversation offers a perspective on why career success depends on more than technical expertise.
-

entry.title: Techer Live: JPL at 90: Caltech, JPL and What's Next

media:group.media:title: Techer Live: JPL at 90: Caltech, JPL and What's Next
media:group.media:description:
In 1936, a small group of Caltech students and self-taught rocketeers tested a rocket motor in the Arroyo Seco. Ninety years later, the Jet Propulsion Laboratory, which Caltech manages for NASA, has sent spacecraft to every planet in the solar system.
In this Techer Live conversation, recorded during Alumni Weekend, three people whose careers span the Lab’s history discuss how the partnership between campus and Lab turns scientific questions into missions. They cover the early days in the Arroyo, Mars landings, AI in space exploration, and how new technology makes it onto a mission.
-
Panelists
Charles Elachi (MS ‘69, PhD ‘71): professor of electrical engineering and planetary science, emeritus, Caltech; JPL director from 2001 to 2016; 2021 Distinguished Alumni Award recipient
Nagin Cox: senior systems engineer, JPL, with roles on missions from Galileo to Perseverance and Europa Clipper
Shouleh Nikzad (MS ‘84, PhD ‘90): chief technologist, JPL; senior faculty associate in physics, Caltech; 2026 Distinguished Alumni Award recipient
Moderator
Casey Dreier: chief of space policy, The Planetary Society
-
Recorded October 17, 2026, in Ramo Auditorium at Caltech.

media:group.media:title: Inaugural Address by President Ray Jayawardhana – October 29, 2026
media:group.media:description:
On October 29, 2026, Ray Jayawardhana was formally inaugurated as Caltech's 10th president. In his inaugural address, President Jayawardhana drew on Caltech's history of scientific daring to outline three aspirations for the Institute's future, grounded in ambitious curiosity, a flourishing community, and sharing the benefits and wonder of discovery with the wider world.

entry.title: The Inauguration of President Ray Jayawardhana

media:group.media:title: The Inauguration of President Ray Jayawardhana
media:group.media:description:
On October 29, 2026, Ray Jayawardhana, renowned astrophysicist, acclaimed author, and transformative leader, was inaugurated as Caltech's 10th president.
The Inauguration of President Jayawardhana celebrates the spirit of First Light—the threshold moment in astronomy when a telescope makes its first observation and opens a new window to discovery. That same spirit of possibility defines the Caltech community. Through curiosity-driven inquiry, powerful experimentation, and groundbreaking instrumentation, Caltech illuminates new fields of knowledge and accelerates breakthroughs that shape the future of science, technology, and society.
Join us in celebrating the next chapter.
Learn more about First Light: The Inauguration of President Ray Jayawardhana: https://inauguration.caltech.edu

entry.title: Artemis II Commander Reid Wiseman joins Caltech and JPL

media:group.media:title: Artemis II Commander Reid Wiseman joins Caltech and JPL
media:group.media:description:
Artemis II commander Reid Wiseman has been named Caltech associate vice president and deputy director of NASA’s Jet Propulsion Laboratory in Southern California. The emeritus astronaut and retired U.S. Navy captain begins his new role at NASA’s center of excellence for robotics and deep space exploration and at Caltech, which manages JPL for NASA, on Nov. 30, 2026.
This video of Reid Wiseman accepting this role was shared at a Brave New Space Age event at Caltech on Oct. 28, 2026.
Learn more: https://www.caltech.edu/about/news/artemis-ii-commander-reid-wiseman-joins-caltech-as-associate-vice-president-and-jpl-deputy-director

entry.title: Watson Lecture Promo – November 4, 2026: Katie Bouman

media:group.media:title: Watson Lecture Promo – November 4, 2026: Katie Bouman
media:group.media:description:
Illuminating the Hidden Universe with Physics and AI with Katie Bouman
Wednesday, November 4, 2026
6 p.m. — Activities and music. Food, drinks, and books available for purchase 7 p.m. — Doors open 7:30 p.m. — Talk and Q&A 8:30 p.m. — Post-talk concessions and conversation.
Some of the most iconic images in modern science were never captured by a camera in the traditional sense. Instead, they were inferred from indirect and incomplete measurements, using a careful combination of physics, prior knowledge, and computation.
In this talk, Katie Bouman will explore how physics and artificial intelligence (AI) are working together to illuminate parts of the universe that are difficult—or even fundamentally impossible—to observe directly. It begins with the story of black hole imaging, where theory long predicted what we should see, and where confidence came not from a single image, but from the consistency of features across many reconstructions of the same data. This kind of inference is not unique to extreme astrophysics, but it also underlies how researchers form images in familiar technologies they rely on every day.
Advance registration for Bouman's talk is full. Guests who have not registered are still welcome to attend the preshow, which does not require registration, beginning at 6 p.m., featuring food, music, and interactive displays. After the preshow, non-ticketed guests interested in attending the talk may join our standby line by 6:50 p.m.
More info: https://www.caltech.edu/campus-life-events/calendar/watson-lecture-katie-bouman

entry.title: Caltech JPL: One Mission. One Partnership.

media:group.media:title: Caltech JPL: One Mission. One Partnership.
media:group.media:description:
Caltech created the Jet Propulsion Laboratory in 1936. Decades in the making, this has brought the United States a long line of firsts. Together, Caltech and JPL advance frontier technologies - including quantum, AI and autonomy, microelectronics, advanced radar and sensing, robotics, and resilient space systems - with applications across civil, defense, intelligence, and commercial sectors. Caltech JPL helps sustain America’s innovation edge and the capabilities essential to long-term strategic advantage.
Learn more: https://www.caltech.edu/research/jpl
